info.bio:
Slowdive es una banda shoegaze que se formó en 1989, separándose hacia 1995. Se formó en Reading, Berkshire (UK) y pronto firmó contrato con Creation Records. El origen del nombre no proviene de la canción de "Siouxsie and the Banshees" como se podría pensar, sino de un sueño del bajista, Nick Chaplin. 

Sus integrantes son Neil Halstead (guitarra y voz), Rachel Goswell (guitarra y voz), Nick Chaplin (bajo), Christian Savill (guitarra), Adrian Sell (batería en 1989), Simon Scott (batería entre 1990 y 1994) e Ian McCutcheon (batería desde 1994). 

Cuando Savill y Chaplin abandonaron la banda después del lanzamiento del disco "Pygmalion" (1995), los miembros restantes formaron "Mojave 3".

En 2014, Slowdive realiza una reunión en forma de gira continental que transcurre en diversos festivales de prestigio. Los rumores de posibles nuevas grabaciones van tomando forma lentamente, hasta que se confirma su siguiente LP de duración extendida, el auto-titulado "Slowdive" (2017) concretando una gira que tomaría diversos festivales y países, ahora mismo la banda busca trabajar en su siguiente 5 trabajo de estudio. 

Discos:
Just for a Day (1991, Creation/SBK)
Souvlaki (1993, Creation; 1994, Creation/SBK [U.S.])
Pygmalion (1995, Creation) 
Slowdive (2017, Dead Oceans)

Singles, EPs:

Morningrise EP (1991)

split tour 7" (Ride: "Leave Them All Behind" b/w Slowdive: "She Calls") (1992) (blue vinyl)

info.wikipedia:
Slowdive es una banda de rock alternativo británica formada en 1989.[1]​ El origen del nombre proviene de un sueño del bajista Nick Chaplin y de una conversación con Rachel Goswell que sugirió a «Slowdive», el nombre de un sencillo de uno de sus grupos preferidos, Siouxsie and the Banshees.[2]​[3]​ El grupo es mayormente conocido por ser uno de los mayores exponentes de los géneros shoegaze y dream pop, y por su álbum Souvlaki (1993), catalogado uno de los tres pilares fundamentales del shoegaze.

Sus integrantes fueron Neil Halstead (guitarra y voz), Rachel Goswell (guitarra y voz), Nick Chaplin (bajo), Christian Savill (guitarra), Adrian Sell (batería en 1989), Simon Scott (batería entre 1990 y 1994) e Ian McCutcheon (batería desde 1994). Cuando Savill y Chaplin dejaron la banda después del lanzamiento del disco Pygmalion (1995), los miembros restantes formaron la banda Mojave 3.

En enero de 2014 anunciaron su retorno tras confirmar actuaciones en el festival realizado en Barcelona Primavera Sound y en Londres. También confirmaron sus intenciones de grabar nuevo material.[4]​ El 5 de mayo de 2017, después de veintidós años, lanzaron un nuevo álbum homónimo.[5]​

scenes.name: Psicodelia británica de los noventa
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La edad de oro de la psicodelia británica no fueron los sesenta sino los noventa: las raves crean una demanda inagotable de música inducida por (o para) las drogas. La versión pop (Telescopes, Inspiral Carpets, Verve, Sundial, Auteurs, Kula Shaker), las más sofisticadas (Curve, Cranberries, Rollerskate Skinny, Beta Band, dEUS, Gorky's Zygotic Mynci), el space-rock libre (Porcupine Tree, Terminal Cheesecake, Heads), los últimos shoegazers (Ride, Swervedriver, Spectrum y E.A.R. de Sonic Boom, Spiritualized de Jason Pierce, Flying Saucer Attack, encuentro de shoegazing y ambient) y el dream-pop (Lush, Pale Saints, Slowdive, Catherine Wheel, Bark Psychosis).

podcast.title: Example of Shoegaze-leaning Dreampop
podcast.body: Slowdive is highlighted as a band that exemplifies how Dreampop can "leak into the Shoegaze world." Their music is characterized by atmosphere, textures, reverb, and echo, but with a potentially more serious attitude and increased volume compared to quieter Dreampop acts, bridging the two genres. "Yes, Dreampop can be quiet like the cocktail twins and Mazzy Star, but it can also leak into the Shougay's world and touch on groups like Slow Dive and My Bloody Valentine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Old School Style Perception
podcast.body: The band's style on their 2017 album was acknowledged as potentially being seen as "old school" or a bit behind the times, appealing mostly to "old school" fans due to their long period of silence. "es un estilo que se ha quedado como muy aparte y como muy de de gente de la vieja escuela."

podcast.title: Outskirts of Britpop
podcast.body: Slow Dive was identified as one of the "shoe-gazer bands" circling the outskirts of the Britpop universe, indicating their concurrent but distinct musical style during the era. "Circling the outskirts of this universe were shoe-gazer bands like My Bloody Valentine and Ride and Lush and Swerve Driver and Slow Dive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock: Chapter 12

podcast.title: Oxford Music Scene
podcast.body: Slowdive was among the "big-ish Oxford bands" that had achieved semi-fame by playing at the Jericho Tavern, the venue where "On a Friday" had a significant gig in October 1991. "the Jericho Tavern, which by the way was semi-famous at the time for hosting other big-ish Oxford bands like Super Grass and Ride and Slow Dive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pioneer of Shoegaze
podcast.body: Slowdive was among the bands that surfaced between 1989 and 1991, adopting and expanding upon My Bloody Valentine's foundation of ethereal melodies and distorted guitars within the Shoegaze genre. Their career was launched by Creation Records. "En seguida, susguieron bandas como Ride, Slowdive, Feltzaint y Lash, quienes tomaron aquella combinación de melodía setéria, guitarras distorsionadas y la llevaron aún más lejos."

srcs.episode: El disco imposible: La historia de Loveless y My Bloody Valentine

podcast.title: Post-Rock Evolution
podcast.body: Initially a shoegaze band, Slowdive's later material began to incorporate elements of post-rock, demonstrating an overlap between the two genres. "Slow dive, definitely Shoegaze, but their later stuff was also very post-rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2

podcast.title: Recommended for Fans
podcast.body: Boards of Canada is highly recommended for fans of Slowdive's dream pop sound. "cualquiera avante del Drimpop de ... Slowdive, de Ride, incluso de Mokuey o de My Lord Ninjaked, va a pasarse, vamos, va a maravillarse con lo que es Borsov Canadá."

srcs.episode: BOARDS OF CANADA. La visión romántica del IDM

podcast.title: Return from Hiatus
podcast.body: Slowdive released their self-titled album in 2017 after many years of silence, a significant return for the band. "han pasado tantos años y tantos años como en silencio."

srcs.episode: Discos que los subsciptores echasteis en falta en la lista de lo mejor del año y tenéis razón

podcast.title: Shoegaze Band Example
podcast.body: Slowdive was mentioned as an example of a Shoegaze band, a loud, fuzzy, buzzy form of guitar rock that emerged from the Thames River Valley in the very late 80s and early 90s. "There were bands like Slow Dive, Chapter House, Curve, Lush, My Bloody Valentine, Adorable, The Catherine Wheel."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Shoegaze Continuation
podcast.body: Slowdive is noted as a band that continued the Shoegaze movement as an independent offshoot from the major 90s movements, extending almost until the mid-1990s and leaving a distinctive sound. "Y seguimos teniendo nombres que a lo mejor han quedado un poco olvidados pero que siguen siendo muy interesantes como puede ser Slow Dive."

xref.title: Post-Graduation Concerts (1991)
xref.body: The band's first concert after their graduation period took place on July 22, 1991, at the Hollywood in Oxford. Despite having played together "off and on for years" and estimated "at least 100 times" before, this gig was described as relatively modest: "five friends, two strobe lights and a smoke machine." A subsequent gig in October at the Jericho Tavern, known for hosting other Oxford bands like Supergrass, Ride, and Slowdive, proved to be a turning point. "The big day that everybody remembers is July 22, 1991. Just when they played a show at the Hollywood in Oxford, their first post-graduation concert."
